title_en: China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, Jinan Office v. Shandong Jinan Medical Procurement and Supply Station, Shandong Medical Group Co., Ltd., and Shandong Medical Company — dispute over loan guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 3 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning Whether the State-owned Allocated Land Use Rights of Bankrupt Enterprises Should Be Included in the Bankruptcy Property, etc., if a building is attached to state-owned land use rights acquired through allocation, and the building and the land are jointly mortgaged, the mortgage of the land use rights must undergo statutory approval procedures; otherwise, the mortgage shall be deemed invalid. When the parties, in concluding the mortgage contract, only agree to mortgage their own real estate and register the mortgage on the building, without simultaneously mortgaging the state-owned allocated land use rights attached to the building, the above provision does not apply.

full_text_en:
China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation

Jinan Office v. Shandong Jinan Medical Procurement and Supply Station,

Shandong Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd., and Shandong Pharmaceutical Company

— dispute over loan guarantee contract

Ruling Summary

According to paragraph 3 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Whether the Right to the Use of State-Owned Allocated Land of a Bankrupt Enterprise Shall Be Included in the Bankruptcy Property, if a building is attached to the right to the use of state-owned land obtained through allocation, and the building and the land are mortgaged together, the mortgage of the right to the use of land must undergo the statutory approval formalities; otherwise, the mortgage shall be deemed invalid. Where, at the time of entering into a mortgage contract, the parties only agree to mortgage the self-owned buildings and register the building mortgage, and do not concurrently mortgage the right to the use of state-owned allocated land to which the buildings are attached, the above provision shall not apply.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2006) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 153

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, Jinan Office, domiciled at No. 168 Jingqi Road, Jinan, Shandong Province.
Person in charge: Hu Jianzhong, General Manager of the Office.
Authorized representatives: Wang Chuangli, staff member of the Office; Li Dongxia, attorney at Beijing Haiming Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Shandong Jinan Medical Procurement and Supply Station, domiciled at No. 21 Weisan Road, Jinan, Shandong Province.
Person in charge: Cui Yiping, Head of the Bankruptcy Liquidation Working Group of the Station.
Authorized representatives: Liu Jian, staff member of the Station; Zhang Yong, staff member of the Station.

Defendant at First Instance: Shandong Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 11 Jiefang Road, Jinan, Shandong Province.
Legal representative: Shi Zhongxi, General Manager of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance: Shandong Pharmaceutical Company, domiciled at No. 11 Jiefang Road, Jinan, Shandong Province.

The Appellant, China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, Jinan Office (hereinafter referred to as Great Wall Company, Jinan Office), appealed to this Court against the Civil Judgment (2006) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 27 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court in the case of dispute over loan guarantee contract with the Respondent, Shandong Jinan Medical Procurement and Supply Station (hereinafter referred to as the Medical Procurement Station), and the Defendants at First Instance, Shandong Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Pharmaceutical Group Company) and Shandong Pharmaceutical Company (hereinafter referred to as the Pharmaceutical Company). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel with Judge Wang Dongmin as Presiding Judge, and Acting Judges Lei Jiping and Li Jingping as members to hear the case. The court clerk was Zhang Yongshu. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found: On December 26, 2003, the Huaiyin Sub-branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Jinan (hereinafter referred to as Huaiyin ICBC) entered into a Loan Contract numbered 2003 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 0197 with the Medical Procurement Station. The contract stipulated that the Medical Procurement Station would borrow RMB 13.8 million from Huaiyin ICBC for a term of 11 months, from December 26, 2003 to November 25, 2004, for the purpose of "repaying the loan principal owed by the borrower to the lender under the Loan Contract No. 2001 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 0007." This loan was a refinancing arrangement; the actual loan amount and date were subject to the loan receipt. The monthly interest rate was 4.425‰, with monthly interest settlement, and overdue interest was charged at 0.21‰ per day. The loan receipt issued by Huaiyin ICBC indicated that the loan was disbursed on December 31, 2003, with a repayment date of November 25, 2004, for the purpose of repaying the loan principal under Contract No. 2001 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 0007, at an interest rate of 4.425‰. The installment repayment record showed a repayment of RMB 10,000 on August 24, 2004. On the same day, Huaiyin ICBC entered into a Guarantee Contract numbered 2003 Huai Qi Xin Bao Zi No. 0197 with the Pharmaceutical Group Company, stipulating that the Pharmaceutical Group Company would provide joint and several liability guarantee for the loan under the above Loan Contract, covering a principal of RMB 13.8 million, including loan principal, interest, compound interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, compensation, costs of enforcing the claim, and all other amounts payable. The guarantee period was two years from the day after the loan maturity. The guarantor's representations and warranties clause stated: "The guarantor fully understands the purpose of the loan of the principal contract borrower and provides the guarantee voluntarily; all its representations are true."

On February 20, 2003, the Medical Procurement Station entered into a Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract numbered 2003 Huai Qi Xin Di Zi No. 0006 with Huaiyin ICBC, stipulating that the borrower, the Medical Procurement Station, would provide mortgage security with its own buildings for loans incurred during the period from March 1, 2003 to March 1, 2006, within a maximum loan balance of RMB 12 million. The mortgage was registered with the Jinan Real Estate Administration Bureau on February 26 of the same year. The land use right on which the mortgaged buildings were situated was for a perpetual term, no land transfer fee had been paid, and it was a state-owned allocated land use right.

On March 27, 2004, Huaiyin ICBC entered into a Loan Contract numbered 2004 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 002 with the Medical Procurement Station. The contract stipulated that the Medical Procurement Station would borrow RMB 12 million from Huaiyin ICBC for a term of 12 months, from March 27, 2004 to March 25, 2005, for the purpose of "repaying the loan principal owed by the borrower to the lender under the Loan Contract No. 2003 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 0006." The monthly interest rate was 4.425‰, with monthly interest settlement, and overdue interest was charged at 0.21‰ per day.

On April 30, 2004, Huaiyin ICBC entered into a Loan Contract numbered 2004 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 005 with the Medical Procurement Station. The contract stipulated that the Medical Procurement Station would borrow RMB 38.3 million from Huaiyin ICBC for a term of 12 months, from April 30, 2004 to April 29, 2005, for the purpose of "repaying the loan principal owed by the borrower to the lender under the Loan Contract No. 2003 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 0027." The monthly interest rate was 4.8675‰, with monthly interest settlement, and overdue interest was charged at 0.21‰ per day. On the same day, Huaiyin ICBC entered into a Guarantee Contract numbered 2004 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 005 with the Pharmaceutical Company, stipulating that the Pharmaceutical Company would provide joint and several liability guarantee for the loan under Loan Contract No. 2004 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 005, covering a principal of RMB 38.5 million, including loan principal, interest, compound interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, compensation, costs of enforcing the claim, and all other amounts payable. The guarantee period was two years from the day after the loan maturity.

On July 23, 2005, the Shandong Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China entered into a Credit Assignment Agreement with Great Wall Company, Jinan Office, agreeing to assign the claims, including the three claims in this case, to Great Wall Company, Jinan Office. On December 22 of the same year, the two parties published a joint announcement of credit assignment and debt collection (Issue No. 8) in the Dazhong Daily, which included the three claims in this case.

Great Wall Company, Jinan Office filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on April 26, 2006, requesting: 1. an order that the Medical Procurement Station repay the loan principal of RMB 64.09 million and interest of RMB 3,604,287.27; 2. confirmation that the Mortgage Contract was valid, and that it had priority to be paid from the mortgaged property; 3. an order that the Pharmaceutical Group Company bear joint and several liability for repayment within the scope of the guarantee.

After trial, the court of first instance held: The three loan contracts in this case were all the true expressions of the parties' intentions, their contents did not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and they were all valid contracts. After Great Wall Company, Jinan Office acquired the claims, it had fulfilled its obligations of notification and collection, and its exercise of rights was lawful and justified. The debtor, the Medical Procurement Station, should repay the outstanding loan principal and interest. However, the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract numbered 2003 Huai Qi Xin Di Zi No. 0006 entered into between the debtor, the Medical Procurement Station, and Huaiyin ICBC stipulated that the Medical Procurement Station would provide mortgage security with its own buildings for loans incurred during the period from March 1, 2003 to March 1, 2006, within a maximum amount of RMB 12 million, and the mortgage was registered with the Real Estate Administration Bureau. Since the mortgaged buildings were situated on state-owned allocated land use rights, and the mortgage contract had not been approved or registered by the land administration department, the mortgage contract was invalid. The court did not support Great Wall Company, Jinan Office's claim for priority to be paid from the mortgaged buildings.

The Guarantee Contract numbered 2003 Huai Qi Xin Bao Zi No. 0197 entered into between the Pharmaceutical Group Company and Huaiyin ICBC stipulated that the Pharmaceutical Group Company would provide joint and several liability guarantee for the loan of RMB 13.8 million under Loan Contract No. 2003 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 0197. This Guarantee Contract did not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, was valid, and the guarantor, the Pharmaceutical Group Company, should bear joint and several liability for the guarantee. RMB 10,000 of principal on this loan had been repaid, so the actual outstanding principal was RMB 13.79 million. The Pharmaceutical Group Company argued that it was not aware that this loan was used for refinancing and should be exempted from liability. Since the Loan Contract clearly stated the purpose of the loan was to repay the loan under the original loan contract, and the guarantor, the Pharmaceutical Group Company, declared in the Guarantee Contract that it "fully understood the purpose of the guaranteed loan," the Pharmaceutical Group Company's defense that it was unaware of the true purpose of the loan and should be exempted from guarantee liability was untenable. As for the Pharmaceutical Group Company's argument that there was a mortgage security for this loan and the guarantor should only bear guarantee liability for debts beyond the scope of the security in rem, because the copy of the registration certificate for the mortgaged property submitted by the Pharmaceutical Group Company was for the mortgage under Contract No. 2001 Huai Qi Xin Di Zi No. 0007, which was not related to this case, and Great Wall Company, Jinan Office did not recognize its evidentiary effect, the evidence submitted by the Pharmaceutical Group Company could not prove that there was another mortgage security for the debt under this loan.

The Pharmaceutical Company guaranteed the loan of RMB 38.3 million under Loan Contract No. 2004 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 005. As the guarantor, the Pharmaceutical Company, had entered bankruptcy proceedings, Great Wall Company, Jinan Office had withdrawn its claims against the guarantor, the Pharmaceutical Company, and instead submitted a claim for the guaranteed debt to the bankruptcy liquidation committee. Any amount recovered by Great Wall Company, Jinan Office in the bankruptcy proceedings of the guarantor, the Pharmaceutical Company, should be deducted from the total debt to be repaid by the principal debtor, the Medical Procurement Station. In summary, the facts of the loan debts in this case were clear. The debtor, the Medical Procurement Station, should repay Great Wall Company, Jinan Office the principal of the three loans totaling RMB 64.09 million and interest of RMB 3,604,287.27. The guarantor, the Pharmaceutical Group Company, should bear joint and several liability for the guarantee for the principal of RMB 13.79 million (being RMB 13.8 million minus the repaid RMB 10,000) and the corresponding interest, in accordance with the Guarantee Contract No. 2003 Huai Qi Xin Bao Zi No. 0197. In accordance with Article 60, Article 206, and Article 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 18 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, and paragraph 3, Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Whether the Right to the Use of State-Owned Allocated Land of a Bankrupt Enterprise Shall Be Included in the Bankruptcy Property, the court ruled: 1. Within ten days after the judgment takes effect, the Medical Procurement Station shall repay Great Wall Company, Jinan Office the loan principal totaling RMB 64.09 million and interest of RMB 3,604,287.27 under Loan Contract No. 2003 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 0197, Loan Contract No. 2004 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 002, and Loan Contract No. 2004 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 005; 2. The Pharmaceutical Group Company shall bear joint and several liability for the guarantee for the outstanding principal of RMB 13.79 million and the corresponding interest under Loan Contract No. 2003 Huai Qi Xin Liu Zi No. 0197; 3. The other claims of Great Wall Company, Jinan Office were dismissed. The court acceptance fee for the first instance was RMB 174,240.7, and the fee for preservation of property was RMB 75,000, both to be borne by the Medical Procurement Station.

The Appellant, Great Wall Company, Jinan Office, disagreed with the civil judgment of the court of first instance and appealed to this Court, arguing: The judgment of the first instance incorrectly applied the law. It requested the reversal of item 3 of the first instance judgment, confirmation that the mortgage contract was valid, and that the Office had priority to be paid. The litigation costs of this case should be borne by the Medical Procurement Station. The main reasons were: 1. The mortgage contract had been lawfully registered, and the formalities were valid, so it should be protected by law. The Medical Procurement Station and Huaiyin ICBC entered into the Loan Contract and the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract, with the Medical Procurement Station providing its own buildings as security. According to Article 61 of the Real Estate Administration Law and Article 42 of the Security Law, and the approvals of the Shandong Provincial People's Government, Lu Zheng Zi 1996 No. 68 and Lu Zheng Zi 2002 No. 267, the real estate transaction authority was designated as the competent authority for registering mortgages on buildings such as factory buildings. Mortgages previously registered with the administrative department for industry and commerce were confirmed as valid. 2. The first instance court incorrectly applied the law and arbitrarily expanded the scope of application of judicial interpretations, harming the national interest represented by the company and deviating from the legislative intent.

The Respondent, the Medical Procurement Station, argued in defense: The facts found by the first instance court were clear, and the law was correctly applied. It requested that the judgment be upheld. Since it had entered bankruptcy proceedings, it requested a stay of the proceedings in this case.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, this Court further found: During the second instance trial of this case, the Huaiyin District People's Court of Jinan City, Shandong Province, declared the Medical Procurement Station bankrupt for debt repayment by Civil Ruling (2007) Huai Min Po Zi No. 1, and appointed an administrator for the bankruptcy case of the Medical Procurement Station.

After trial, this Court held that this case is a dispute over a loan and guarantee. The focus of the dispute between the parties in the second instance was: How to determine the validity of the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract in question, and whether the creditor had priority to be paid. In this case, on February 20, 2003, the Medical Procurement Station entered into the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract with Huaiyin ICBC, explicitly agreeing to mortgage only its own buildings, and subsequently only registered the mortgage with the local real estate administration department. These actions occurred before the Property Law of the People's Republic of China took effect, so the laws and regulations in effect at that time should apply. The above Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract was the true expression of the parties' intentions, its contents did not violate the prohibitive provisions of Chinese laws and administrative regulations, and the buildings mortgaged by the mortgagor, the Medical Procurement Station, were its own buildings, and the registration authority was the Jinan Real Estate Administration Bureau, which complied with Article 41 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Security Law): "Where the parties mortgage property as specified in Article 42 of this Law, they shall register the mortgaged property; the mortgage contract shall take effect from the date of registration." Therefore, whether the mortgagor, the Medical Procurement Station, separately handled the registration procedures for the right to the use of state-owned land did not affect the validity of the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract. This Court determined that the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract was legal and valid, and the mortgage right was established. The Appellant's ground of appeal that the mortgage contract was valid and the mortgage right should be enforced had factual and legal basis, and this Court supported it.

Article 3 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Whether the Right to the Use of State-Owned Allocated Land of a Bankrupt Enterprise Shall Be Included in the Bankruptcy Property (hereinafter referred to as the Interpretation) provides: "If a building is attached to the right to the use of state-owned land obtained through allocation, and the building and the land are mortgaged together, the mortgage of the right to the use of land must undergo the statutory approval formalities; otherwise, the mortgage shall be deemed invalid." The phrase "the building and the land are mortgaged together" in the Interpretation refers to the situation where the parties agree to mortgage the building and the land together. If, at the time of entering into the contract, the parties agree to mortgage the building together with the right to the use of state-owned allocated land, then the mortgagor must undergo the statutory approval formalities for the mortgaged right to the use of state-owned land. In this case, the parties entered into a contract agreeing only to mortgage the self-owned buildings and register the building mortgage, without involving the concurrent mortgage of the land use right. This fact does not match the situation described in the above Interpretation. The first instance judgment's reliance on that Interpretation to declare the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract invalid was improper, and this Court hereby corrects it.

Given that the Medical Procurement Station has been ruled by a people's court to enter bankruptcy proceedings, in accordance with Article 20 of the Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China: "After the people's court accepts the bankruptcy application, a civil action or arbitration concerning the debtor that has already commenced but has not yet been concluded shall be suspended; the action or arbitration shall continue after the administrator takes over the debtor's property." This action should continue. The Medical Procurement Station's argument in its defense that this case should be suspended is not supported by this Court. After this Court determines that the above Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract is valid, the mortgagee, Great Wall Company, Jinan Office, may submit an application to the administrator of the Medical Procurement Station's bankruptcy case to exercise its priority right in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Bankruptcy Law. However, this right shall be realized within the scope of the proceeds from the sale or auction of the mortgaged buildings involved in this case (excluding the proceeds from the land use right on which the buildings are situated), and the maximum amount shall not exceed the maximum amount of RMB 12 million stipulated in the mortgage contract.

In summary, the facts found by the first instance judgment were clear, but the application of law was improper. In accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, items (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm items 1 and 2 of the Civil Judgment (2006) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 27 of the Shandong High People's Court;
2. Amend item 3 of the Civil Judgment (2006) Lu Min Er Chu Zi No. 27 of the Shandong High People's Court to: China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, Jinan Office, has priority to be paid from the self-owned buildings mortgaged by Shandong Jinan Medical Procurement and Supply Station under the Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract No. 2003 Huai Qi Xin Di Zi No. 0006, with the maximum amount not exceeding RMB 12 million.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance was RMB 174,240.7, and the fee for preservation of property was RMB 75,000, to be borne by Shandong Jinan Medical Procurement and Supply Station. The court acceptance fee for the second instance was RMB 174,240.7, to be borne by Shandong Jinan Medical Procurement and Supply Station.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Dongmin
Acting Judge: Lei Jiping
Acting Judge: Li Jingping

December 14, 2007

Court Clerk: Zhang Yongshu

Profile of the Presiding Judge

Wang Dongmin, Senior Judge: Born in 1964, Master of Laws, served as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court from 2004.
